person.name: Joel Abad
person.traits: Six months into a site contract, sends the fifteenth's pay home. Angrier at himself than at the caller. Gives you exactly the time he said he would.

harmed.prompt: Joel meets you at the site gate in a hi-vis vest and does not take it off. "Twenty minutes. Then I've got a pour." He looks at the road rather than at you. "I know what it was. I knew about an hour after. You don't need to tell me what it was."
harmed.note: You took the money he sends home. He is angrier at himself than at the caller, and he has decided the way to carry it is to have no time for it.

resistant.prompt: "You're the detective." Joel walks you in past the mixer with the number still faintly on the back of his hand in marker. "I rang the real office from the site phone while he was still talking on mine. A woman laughed at me. Then she took the number down." He is almost cheerful about it.
resistant.note: He refused the call you made and checked in the same minute. There is nothing to trace, and a good deal to say.

unfinished.prompt: "Somebody said warrant, and then the line went." Joel says it at the gate, not quite letting you in. "I've been waiting for a letter. Nothing's come." He looks at you as if you might be the letter.
unfinished.note: Your call to him never finished. He half believes there is a case, and he has been braced for a knock at the gate for weeks.

evidence.label: The Reference Number
evidence.description: Copied off the back of his hand onto a cement bag in the site office: 2024-0417, and under it the name of the desk the caller gave and the account it was to be paid to.
evidence.tactic: Impersonating an authority: a reference number sounds like a file, and a file sounds like an office - it cost the caller nothing to invent.

evidence.label: Cash-in Slip
evidence.description: From the remittance counter on the corner: P16,000 to an account in a personal name, 3:41 that afternoon - nineteen minutes before the officer was due at the site.
evidence.tactic: Manufactured fear: an officer at the gate in front of his crew, with a deadline measured in minutes, so that paying felt cheaper than checking.

evidence.label: Site Office Phone Log
evidence.description: The site phone's log for that afternoon: an outgoing call to the revenue office's published number at 3:12, four minutes long, while his own phone was still on the other line.
evidence.tactic: Denying time to check: the check that ended it took four minutes on a second phone - which is why the caller said the desk could only hold the warrant while they were talking.

evidence.label: Site Payslip
evidence.description: His payslip for the fifteenth, from the contractor: the amount, the deductions, the tax paid through the company.

ask_call.prompt: "Enforcement desk, revenue office. He had a case number - it's there, on the bag. He had my tax number. He had the contractor's name." Joel counts them off on his fingers. "And an officer coming to the site at four. That was the bit. Not the money. An officer at the gate in front of the crew." He looks up. "Nobody from the government has ever telephoned me in my life. I knew that. I knew it while he was talking."

tactic_quiz.setup: You read the call back to him the way he told it: an enforcement desk, a reference number, his own tax number, and [i]an officer is dispatched to your site at four unless it is settled by phone before then.[/i]
tactic_quiz.question: Which part of that would a real government office never do?

milestone.title: Tactic Identified: The Office That Never Calls
milestone.detail: Recognized that a genuine authority writes, gives you a way to contest, and takes payment only at its own counters - a fine payable by phone, to a personal account, on a deadline of hours, is the impersonation, whatever number it quotes.

options.text: Take payment over the phone, to a personal account, on a deadline measured in hours.
options.feedback: That is the line no office crosses. A real assessment arrives in writing, names a counter or a bank, and gives you a way to dispute it - weeks, not minutes. Everything else in the call is cheap to fake: a reference number is a string of digits, a tax number and an employer are on any bought list. The deadline is the tell, because a real process is slow on purpose.

options.text: Telephone a taxpayer at his place of work.
options.feedback: Rare, and worth suspicion, but not impossible - and a caller can always say it was a courtesy. What settles it is not the call but what the call wants: money, now, by a route no office uses.
Real offices quote reference numbers constantly - which is exactly why a fake one works. A number is the cheapest thing to invent. Judge the call by what it asks for, never by how official it sounds.
Governments do enforce, and they say so - in writing, after notices, with a way to appeal. The threat is not what was wrong. The threat with a phone payment attached and an afternoon to comply is.

ask_evidence.evidence_hint: He remembers the reference number to the digit. What you need is where the money went, and when.
